guide.q.owner_vs_manager: What's the difference between an owner and a manager?
guide.a.owner_vs_manager:
Owners can do everything, including sending refunds and approving payment checks.

Managers can look after listings and groups, see the calendar and activity log, and refresh payment status. They cannot send refunds, approve payment checks, change settings, manage users, questions or holidays, make API keys, edit site pages, or look at who is signed in.
guide.a.editor_role:
Editors only write content. They can create and change listings and groups, and edit public site pages when the Site feature is on.

Editors cannot see attendees, income, costs, or Money. They cannot change settings, manage users, or use the API. An editor holds no key for reading attendee details, so personal data stays protected.
guide.q.agent_role: What can a Delivery agent do?
guide.a.agent_role: Delivery agents see only their own delivery run sheet (/admin/deliveries) — the drop-offs and collections for the delivery vans they are assigned to. They cannot open any other admin page.
guide.a.scanner_role:
Scanners work at the door. After signing in they see the Scanner doors page, which lists a scanner link for every listing and group. There they can scan tickets with the camera, check people in by hand, and check people out on a ticket's own check-in page.

Scanners cannot open any other admin page: no attendee lists, settings, money, or user management.
guide.q.invite_admin: How do I invite another admin?
guide.a.invite_admin:
Go to Users, enter a username, and choose their role: owner, manager, editor, delivery agent, or scanner.

You receive an invite link. Send it to them. They use the link to set their password and activate their account.
guide.q.invite_link_expiry: How long do invite links last?
guide.a.invite_link_expiry: Invite links expire after 7 days. If the link expires before they use it, delete the pending user and make a new invite.
guide.a.attendee_data_protection: Everything personal — names, email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses — is scrambled before it is saved. Even someone who stole the whole database could not read it without the keys. The data is unlocked only when a signed-in admin views it.
guide.a.encryption_overview:
Encryption means scrambling data so only the right key can read it. Different kinds of data get different treatment, so the site stays both safe and usable:

  • Attendee contact details are protected twice, and one of the keys is your password. Names, email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses, and the free-text answers people type into booking questions are locked with two keys at once — the server's key and a key made from your account password. A thief with a stolen copy of the database and the server's key still cannot read them. Only an admin signed in with their password can unlock them. Pre-set multiple-choice answers are saved as a reference and locked with the server's key, like the listing details below.
  • Listing details are locked in the database. Listing names, descriptions, locations, dates, images and links are scrambled with the server's key before they are written. The stored database never holds them in readable form.
  • Numbers are left readable on purpose. Figures like income and remaining places are stored as plain values, because the database has to add them up and compare them. They hold nothing personal, so keeping them readable lets reports and place checks run without unlocking anything.
guide.q.privacy_first_by_default: Why is this privacy-first instead of a CRM?
guide.a.privacy_first_by_default:
A CRM is a system that profiles customers. This one deliberately stops short of that. It keeps the booking data you need, locks attendee details, and recognises returning customers only through a code that cannot be turned back into their email or phone.

That design protects attendees and you: it does not remove your legal duties, but it shrinks the amount of personal data you are responsible for, which makes GDPR easier to follow. If you want a fuller CRM, listing webhooks are a good place to start — send booking events to a system built for that job.
guide.q.lost_password: What happens if I lose my password?
guide.a.lost_password:
There is no way to recover a lost password. If you lose it, you cannot log in. Keep it somewhere safe.

Another owner can delete your account and send you a fresh invite. All attendee data stays readable for the other admins.
guide.a.export_attendee_data:
Yes. On any listing's attendee list, click Export CSV. A CSV is a simple spreadsheet file that opens in Excel or Google Sheets.

The export includes name, email, phone, address, special instructions, quantity, registration date, amount paid, transaction ID, check-in status, ticket token, and ticket link. Each custom booking question gets its own column, with each attendee's answer.

For daily listings, the attendee list has a date filter — pick a date to see only that day's attendees, and the CSV export follows the same filter.
guide.a.reset_database:
It deletes everything, for good: all listings, attendees, groups, questions, users, holidays, API keys, activity logs, payment set-up, and sign-ins. The site returns to the state it was in when it was brand new.

You must type a confirmation phrase to proceed. This cannot be undone.
guide.a.what_are_webhooks:
A webhook is an automatic message this site sends to another website every time someone books. The message contains the attendee's details.

People use them to connect other tools — for example posting a message in Slack, or adding a row to a spreadsheet.
guide.q.setup_webhook: How do I set up a webhook?
guide.a.setup_webhook:
Add a webhook address when you create or edit a listing. Every time someone books that listing, this site sends the attendee's details to that address.

This one is for your web builder, not for everyday use — the address has to be a service set up to receive these messages.

If one booking would send to more than 16 different addresses, none of them are sent. A delivery failure is recorded in the activity log.

guide.a.what_are_sessions: A session starts each time an admin logs in. Sessions expire after 24 hours. You can see every active session on the Sessions page.
guide.a.what_is_calendar:
The Calendar page lets you pick a date and see every attendee booked on that day, across all listings. This is especially useful for daily listings.

You can download the day's attendees as a CSV, and check people in, edit, or delete them from the same view.
guide.a.what_is_activity_log:
The Log page records what admins did, in order: listing creations, listing changes, attendee changes, question changes.

Both owners and managers can read it. Each listing also has its own log, on the listing's page, showing only what happened to that listing.
guide.q.why_am_i_locked_out_even_though: Why am I locked out even though my password is correct?
guide.a.why_am_i_locked_out_even_though:
You have probably tripped the safety lock after earlier wrong tries. The lock applies to your IP address — roughly, the internet connection you are using — not to your account. Other admins elsewhere are not affected.

Wait 15 minutes and try again.
guide.q.is_there_a_way_to_recover_a: Is there a way to recover a lost password?
guide.a.is_there_a_way_to_recover_a:
No. There is no password recovery. All attendee data is locked with keys made from admin passwords, so a reset would make the data unreadable.

If you lose your password, another owner can delete your account and send a fresh invite. All attendee data stays readable for the other admins. Keep your password somewhere safe.
guide.q.how_are_admin_sessions_secured: How are admin sign-ins kept safe?
guide.a.how_are_admin_sessions_secured:
Sign-ins use cookies that websites are not allowed to read, so a bad page cannot steal one. Each sign-in expires after 24 hours, then you must log in again.

You can see every active sign-in, and end all the others, on the Sessions page — useful if you think someone else has got into your account.
guide.q.how_do_i_log_out_other_users: How do I log out other users?
guide.a.how_do_i_log_out_other_users:
On the Sessions page, click Log out of all other sessions. This ends every session except your own, so all other admins must log in again.

Use it if you think someone else has got into an account.
guide.q.what_happens_if_i_enter_the_wron: What happens if I enter the wrong password?
guide.a.what_happens_if_i_enter_the_wron:
After 5 wrong tries from the same place, that place is blocked from logging in for 15 minutes. During the block, every attempt is refused — even with the right password.

Wait for the block to pass, then try again.
guide.q.what_happens_when_i_change_my_pa: What happens when I change my password?
guide.a.what_happens_when_i_change_my_pa:
Changing your password ends every sign-in for your account. You and anyone else signed in as you must sign in again with the new password.

Your attendee data all stays readable. The data key is re-wrapped with the new password, so records from before the change unlock again once you are back in.
